title: Laser Guide Star at the VLT
caption: The Very Large Telescope and a laser guide star beam, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The view runs down one of the rail tracks used by the Auxiliary Telescopes, leading the eye to the four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope. From the enclosure on the far right, a bright orange beam of a Laser Guide Star shoots into the night, washing the site in a warm glow.
The tracks belong to the smaller Auxiliary Telescopes, which, as the rails suggest, are designed to travel across the platform rather than stay fixed in one place.

The orange beam has a separate purpose. It creates an artificial star high in the atmosphere, a reference point that lets the telescope measure and correct for the blurring caused by turbulent air. That correction, called adaptive optics, sharpens the images the VLT can capture from the ground.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye, so the beam and its glow on the site may appear brighter than they would in person.
